sector: Consumer Defensive (Packaged Foods - shelf-stable, frozen, spices)
drawdown_context: Leveraged-acquirer-of-orphan-brands packaged food roll-up (Crisco, Green Giant, Cream of Wheat, Ortega, Dash, Spices & Seasonings) carrying $2.044B long-term debt against ~$295M adjusted EBITDA. FY24 net sales -6.3% to $1.93B; base business -3.3%; net loss $(251.3)M driven by $320M intangible impairment (Green Giant, Victoria, Static Guard, McCann's) plus $70.6M goodwill impairment (Frozen & Vegetables reporting unit). Dividend already cut from $1.615 (FY22) to $0.76 annual (53% reduction) but maintained at $0.19/qtr through Q1'25. Total stockholders' equity collapsed from $835M to $525M in one year, with APIC at $0 (zero) - dividends now paid from retained earnings. TTM Adj EBITDA at Q1'25 = ~$279.5M; net debt $1.94B; leverage ratio ~6.96x against 7.00x maintenance covenant - 0.04 turn cushion to covenant breach, which would also block the dividend (dividend payment requires <7.00x leverage). The FY24 10-K narrative ('compelling brand portfolio,' 'managing the cost structure') does not flag the proximity to covenant.

rfm_tuples.R: 'The credit agreement provides that our maximum consolidated leverage ratio ... is 7.00 to 1.00. We are also required to maintain a consolidated interest coverage ratio ... of at least 1.75 to 1.00. As of December 28, 2024, we were in compliance with all of the covenants, including the financial covenants, in the credit agreement.' Repeated verbatim in Q1'25 10-Q for March 29, 2025.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode-B distress derivation: compute the ACTUAL ratios using disclosed Adjusted EBITDA and net debt and compare to covenant cushion. FY24 Adj EBITDA $295.4M, FY23 $318.0M, Q1'25 $59.1M, Q1'24 $75.0M. Long-term debt $2,005.6M Q1'25, cash $61.2M = net debt $1,944M. TTM Adj EBITDA at Q1'25 = $295.4 - $75.0 + $59.1 = $279.5M.
rfm_tuples.M_value: FY24 leverage = $1,964M net debt / $295.4M = 6.65x (0.35 turn cushion to 7.00x covenant). Q1'25 TTM leverage = $1,944M / $279.5M = 6.96x (0.04 turn cushion). FY24 interest coverage = $295.4 / $157.4 = 1.88x (0.13 turn cushion to 1.75x). Q1'25 Adj EBITDA -21% YoY. Annualizing the Q1'25 $59.1M run-rate yields $236.5M = 8.22x leverage = COVENANT BREACH. Same threshold also gates dividend payments per credit agreement: 'our credit agreement does not permit us to pay dividends unless we maintain... a consolidated leverage ratio of not more than 7.00 to 1.00.' This is a forced-dividend-suspension setup if Q2/Q3 EBITDA does not recover. NEITHER the 10-K NOR the 10-Q quantifies the cushion or warns shareholders that dividend continuity is mechanically contingent on EBITDA stabilization.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The single highest-conviction signal in the file. Compliance language is technically true at the measurement dates, but the actual cushion is 0.04 turns at Q1'25 and the trailing trajectory points to imminent breach. Management does not disclose the actual ratio or the implied dividend-suspension risk anywhere in MD&A. This is the textbook framework target: technically-compliant narrative concealing mechanical proximity to a covenant and a forced capital action.

Walmart concentration rising QoQ (30.3% FY24 -> 31.4% Q1'25); Walmart receivables concentration 36.0% > sales concentration 30.3% (5.7pt gap) -> Walmart paying slower than other customers OR taking outsized recent shipments. Top-10 = 62.7% of sales. Top-10 receivables = 68.2% (5.5pt gap). Mode-B test: does this concentration explain part of the FY24 volume decline?

Walmart receivables 36.0% vs sales 30.3% = 5.7 percentage-point gap implying Walmart is ~28 days slower paying than the company average (or BGS pushed inventory into Walmart late in the quarter). Top-10 receivables 68.2% vs sales 62.7% = 5.5pt gap = receivables collection risk tilted toward big retailers. Volume declined 2.6% in FY24 base business AND 8.9% in Q1'25 base business - accelerating; concentration is rising into a declining business which is the dangerous combination for CPG distress (one Walmart SKU rationalization could trigger material EBITDA loss -> covenant breach).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: 30%+ Walmart concentration with rising receivables-vs-sales gap is a classic CPG distress vector. Mode-B framework view: BGS is structurally exposed to a single retailer's category-management decisions, and that retailer is reducing inventories and increasing private-label emphasis (the 10-K acknowledges this dynamic). Combined with covenant compression (C1), one Walmart SKU rationalization could break the dividend. Management discloses the concentration but does NOT quantify the EBITDA sensitivity to a Walmart change.

rfm_tuples.R: 'For fiscal 2024 and fiscal 2023, we had cash flows from operating activities of $130.9 million and $247.8 million, respectively, and distributed $60.0 million and $56.0 million as dividends, respectively. Based on our current intended dividend rate of $0.76 per share per annum ... we expect our aggregate dividend payments in 2025 to be approximately $60.6 million.' 'B&G Foods has determined that for fiscal 2024 and fiscal 2023, 100.0% of distributions paid on common stock were treated as a return of capital and 0.0% were treated as a taxable dividend paid from earnings and profits.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode-B dividend-quality and history test. Compare (a) cash from ops trajectory FY22 $279M -> FY23 $247.8M -> FY24 $130.9M (-47% YoY); (b) dividend history FY22 $1.615/share -> FY23 $0.76 (53% cut) -> FY24 $0.76 (held); (c) the 100% return-of-capital tax characterization (no earnings & profits coverage) for two years running; (d) APIC balance: $0 at FY24 (zero) because all paid-in-capital has been distributed as return-of-capital - dividends now come from retained earnings.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Cash from ops FY22 $279M -> FY23 $247.8M -> FY24 $130.9M = -47% YoY. Dividend cut already taken in 2023 (53% from $1.615 to $0.76). FY24 dividends $60.0M = 46% of CFFO (was 23% FY23). For FY25 expected $60.6M dividend vs Q1'25 CFFO $52.7M run-rate of ~$210M - coverage ~29% IF no further EBITDA decline. Retained earnings $528.8M FY24 down from $785.1M FY23 - eroded $256M in one year. 100% of distributions treated as return of capital both years = company has paid dividends out of accumulated paid-in-capital, not earnings, since the 53% cut. rfm_tuples.interpretation: The framework's classic distress fingerprint: dividend already cut 53%, current dividend funded 100% from return-of-capital not earnings, APIC fully eroded, CFFO down 47% YoY, and covenant cushion 0.04 turns. The 10-K's reassurance - 'we expect our aggregate dividend payments in 2025 to be approximately $60.6 million' - is technically a target, not a commitment, but management does not disclose the mechanical conditional. rfm_tuples.R: 'On October 9, 2024, we redeemed in full all $265.4 million remaining aggregate principal amount of our 5.25% senior notes due 2025 at a cash redemption price of 100.0%.' 'On July 12, 2024, we issued an additional $250.0 million aggregate principal amount of our 8.00% senior secured notes due 2028 at a price of 99.502%.' Coupon shift from 5.25% to 8.00% on $250M = 275bps incremental annual cash interest. Net interest expense FY24 $157.4M vs FY23 $151.3M (+$6.1M, +4.0%).
rfm_tuples.f: Mode-B refinancing-cost test. Compute the implied marginal cost of debt and the effective cost-of-capital signal. BGS refinanced 5.25% notes with 8.00% notes - 275bp premium AND a senior secured layer (the prior 2025 notes were senior unsecured, the new 2028 notes are senior secured). This is the credit-market pricing tell: the market demanded both a higher coupon AND collateral.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Coupon escalation: 5.25% -> 8.00% = +275 bps. Tenor extension: 2025 -> 2028 (3 years). Security upgrade: unsecured -> senior secured (subordinating existing 5.25% 2027 notes to the new 2028 secured notes). Issue price 99.502% = additional 50bps of discount = ~8.13% effective yield. Revolver pricing: SOFR + ~250-300bps depending on leverage ratio = 6.32%-6.48% in FY24/Q1'25. Weighted-average cost of debt now ~7%+ vs blended ~5.5% at FY22. Refinancing implies the market would NOT extend BGS unsecured debt at sub-6% coupons - i.e., the market views BGS as a high-yield/distressed credit, contradicting the 10-K's investment-grade-style narrative.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: BGS had to pay 275bps more AND pledge security to refinance $250M of debt in mid-2024 - this is the bond market pricing BGS as distressed even before the Q4 impairment cycle. The 10-K disclosure is technically complete (rates and amounts are stated) but does not characterize the security upgrade or the implication that next refinancing (5.25% notes due Sept 2027) will likely require further coupon escalation or equity dilution. Tranche B term loan ($450M due Oct 2029) refinanced into a new credit agreement structure. Refinance wall pivots to 2027-2029.

rfm_tuples.R: 'Our $550.0 million of 5.25% senior notes due 2027 mature on September 15, 2027, our $799.3 million of 8.00% senior secured notes due 2028 mature on September 15, 2028, our $475.0 million revolving credit facility matures on December 16, 2028, and our $450.0 million of tranche B term loans mature on October 10, 2029.' Compare to (a) current market access (8.00% secured was already required in 2024 for unsecured refi); (b) ATM equity used $73.6M in 2023; (c) APIC fully eroded -> equity issuance dilutes hard at current ~$5-7 price; (d) divestiture options largely exhausted (Back to Nature and Green Giant U.S. shelf-stable already sold).
rfm_tuples.M_value: Sept 2027 maturity: $550M (5.25% unsecured). If market requires 8%+ secured refinancing, BGS faces ~$15M of incremental annual interest on a $550M secured refi (~3% rate jump) - pulling Adj EBITDA cushion further into covenant breach territory. Alternative paths: (i) Asset sales - most monetizable brands (Crisco $320M trademark book, Green Giant frozen) - Crisco sale would lose ~$170M of segment EBITDA = covenant breach mechanically. (ii) Equity raise via ATM - but at $5-7/share, raising $200M would require 30-40M shares = 38-50% dilution. (iii) Debt restructuring - distressed-exchange territory. Risk factors include the boilerplate 'sales of assets; sales of equity; and negotiations with our lenders or noteholders to restructure the applicable debt' - this is the standard playbook for distressed pre-restructuring filers.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The 2027 maturity wall combined with deteriorating credit-market access, dilutive equity-issuance economics, and exhausted monetizable assets is the strategic dead-end the framework is built to detect. The 10-K acknowledges all the contingency options as risk factors but does not characterize the probability or sequencing. The company is one bad quarter from covenant breach and ~28 months from a $550M maturity wall it cannot economically refinance at current credit quality.

summary: BGS at the 2025-05-15 cutoff is a leveraged-acquirer CPG distress case with covenant cushion at the breaking point. The single highest-conviction Mode-B finding: TTM Q1'25 leverage ~6.96x against a 7.00x maintenance covenant (0.04 turn cushion), with Q1'25 Adjusted EBITDA -21% YoY and all four segments declining (volume decline accelerated 3.4x from -2.6% FY24 to -8.9% Q1'25). The same 7.00x covenant gates dividend payments - meaning the $0.76 annual dividend is mechanically at-risk on either covenant breach or board discretion to preserve cash. Forward impairment risk is elevated: FY24 $390.6M of impairments already taken; Frozen & Vegetables segment turned EBITDA-negative in Q1'25 with $548M of goodwill on book, and Crisco ($320M trademark carrying value) sits in the most commoditized, private-label-vulnerable aisle with Walmart as 31.4% of sales. Disclosure-quality red flag: the Q1'25 10-Q contains literal bracketed placeholder text ('[NOTE: To be updated, especially with respect to China.]' plus segment commentaries) that the CFO SOX 302 certified - a tangible internal-control discipline indicator. Mitigants: stable management team (CEO since 2021, CFO since 2017), KPMG auditor since 1996 with active dual-CAM treatment of impairments, no near-term debt wall (next maturity Sept 2027), $61M cash + $225M revolver capacity. Verdict: SHORT-tier under the honesty-alpha framework - the 10-K narrative ('compelling brand portfolio,' 'managing the cost structure,' 'fiscal 2025 we expect aggregate dividend payments of $60.6M') is technically compliant but mechanically falsified by the covenant math and Q1'25 segment collapse. Dividend suspension and incremental impairment are base-case 12-month outcomes.
